"Furthermore, good son!

If there are sentient beings who desire to read and recite various treatises in order to subdue other beings—namely, those treatises which may have been spoken by the Buddha, or spoken by Bodhisattvas, or spoken by Śrāvakas, or spoken by worldly people."

This person should, during the final watch of the night, bathe themselves until clean, put on fresh and pure garments, burn solid black aloeswood and tagara incense, and, giving rise to a heart of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings, face the eastern direction with palms joined in utmost sincerity, invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, and then recite this dhāraṇī mantra:
“*Āniruddha-vijaye, bhadra-vijaye, yāpana-vijaye, vatsami, pāṭalāvijaye, tapanavijaye, saptatālagarbhanidhi-kṣema, mahākāruṇika, svāhā.*” “O son of good family!
This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha immediately causes that person to obtain the power of mindfulness and retention so as not to forget. "Good son!..."

If there are sentient beings who wish to enter the great ocean, who wish to engage in trade, who wish to take medicinal decoctions to seek their efficacy, who wish to be freed from bonds, who wish to be released from shackles and fetters, who wish to avoid the transport of goods, or who suffer from the pain of being separated from loved ones or encountering those they hate; or who wish to avoid water and fire, who wish to avoid thieves and bandits, who wish to avoid lions, tigers, wolves, and venomous snakes, who wish to escape the afflictions of disease, hunger, and thirst, or who wish to seek a position of honor—should they have such various desires and petitions, by invoking the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja and reverently making offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, all their wishes shall be fulfilled.
"Furthermore, noble son!

If there is a prince who craves the royal throne and desires to receive the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) to attain sovereign power, he should, during the final watch of the night, bathe himself until clean and put on fresh, pure garments. He should burn solid black *agaru* (aloe) and *tagara* incense, give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings, and facing the eastern direction with palms joined in utmost sincerity, invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja and recite this dhāraṇī mantra: [The dhāraṇī follows]"
“*Ānīlajaṃbū kaṃboja-pārasīka-bāhlika | bhoṭṭa-sīmāntika-pāṭaliputra-jambū | tāmraparṇī śātakaumbha-lohita-nirbhāsa-mahākāruṇika svāhā.*” “O son of good family!...”

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha shall cause all those people to fulfill their wishes. "Furthermore, noble son, if there is a community of Brahmins who desire to attain the status of a Great Brahmin,

or if there are sentient beings who seek the status of a householder, or a lay devotee (*gṛhapati*), or a craftsman, or one of great learning, or one of great power, or one of contemplation, or one of liberation— they should, during the final watch of the night, bathe themselves clean, put on fresh and pure garments, burn solid black aloeswood and tagara incense, and, giving rise to a mind of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings, face the eastern direction with palms joined in sincerity, invoke the name of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, and speak these words:"
“May you grant me the power of great compassion, so that what I seek may be swiftly fulfilled.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, having heard that request with his pure divine ear, manifested various forms according to what was appropriate and preached the Dharma for him, causing all his aspirations to be fully satisfied.
"Good son! This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha has accomplished such inconceivable skillful means and wisdom, and has long since entered the ocean of the Buddha’s merits."

"Good son! It may be possible for someone to know the number of drops in the waters of the great ocean, but no one can measure the limit of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha’s skillful means and wisdom in bringing sentient beings to maturity."
Furthermore, son of good family!

The measure of empty space may yet be known, but there is no one who can know the various sentient beings matured by the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, nor his transformations—whether manifesting in the form of a Buddha, a Bodhisattva, a Pratyekabuddha, a Śrāvaka, a Brahmin, or in the forms of boys, girls, or even humans and non-humans—each according to what is appropriate, causing them to be seen with the eyes or encountered in dreams.

If there are sentient beings who, at the time of their death—except for the final, most subtle single breath—have previously committed evil karma that burns away all roots of goodness and would otherwise fall into the evil realms.
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha is capable of rescuing all beings and establishing them upon the path of devas and humans; such are the limits of his deeds.
"Good son! This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, who has accomplished such inconceivable skillful means, has long ago entered the ocean of the Buddha's merits."
"Good son! For this reason, there is a wish-fulfilling jewel upon his crown, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of Śakrābhilagna jewels, emitting a great radiance."

When the Tathāgata had spoken this Dharma, the entire great assembly was filled with wonder and marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence; they all joined their palms and turned toward the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his palms joined, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"Now, this world is possessed of the five turbidities and its sentient beings are ignorant and dark.
How is it that the World-Honored One is able to perform the Buddha-work therein?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
“Good son! You see that space is free from greed, hatred, and delusion, and is pure by nature; yet you regard it as impure because of the obstructions of wind, dust, and darkness.”
Once it has become clear and bright, one immediately perceives the sun, moon, and stars, and understands the temporal measures of *kṣaṇas*, *lava-s*, and *muhūrtas*.

Noble son, the Tathāgata has long attained mastery over the emptiness of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*). He sees that all phenomena are devoid of greed, hatred, and delusion; they are neither bound nor liberated, being pure by their very nature. It is only because sentient beings are shrouded and obstructed by adventitious afflictions (*āgantuka-kleśa*) that they are unable to awaken to this.

The Tathāgata, out of compassion, employs skillful means to preach the Dharma for their sake, in order to sever and eliminate adventitious afflictions, to open their eye of wisdom so they may behold the pure sun of the Tathāgata’s illumination, and to enable them to perceive in the present the profound and wondrous Dharma—the teachings on the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path—thereby establishing and stabilizing all sentient beings therein. Furthermore, he causes them to swiftly resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, to attain great loving-kindness and compassion, and even to become fully endowed with the eighteen unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*), thereby perfecting the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākāra-jñatā*).
"Good son! When a Tathāgata appears in the world, he is able to bring to maturity the assembly of bodhisattvas, as well as the assemblies of pratyekabuddhas and śrāvakas. Good son!"
Now, does this space depend upon the eye?
Does it depend upon the visual consciousness?
Or does it abide by depending upon visual contact?
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja addressed the Buddha, saying: “No,
World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said,
“Good son, does one rely on emptiness because those three feelings arise from the condition of internal eye-contact?”
The Bodhisattva Gaganagañja addressed the Buddha, saying: “No,
World-Honored One.”
The Buddha said:
"Good son, the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are also like this."
The Buddha said,
"Good son! Do sentient beings now rely upon emptiness?"
"Is it that empty space depends upon sentient beings?
The Bodhisattva Gaganagañja addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
Each depends upon the others to mutually constitute objects of perception, yet each also does not constitute an object for the others.
All phenomena are entirely empty and quiescent; all phenomena are entirely false and provisional; all phenomena rely entirely upon Suchness and the Reality Limit (bhūtakoṭi).
World-Honored One!

It is just as empty space is without destruction or formation, without recollection or conceptualization, without movement or agitation, without love or hatred, without sprouts or seeds, without fruit, without karma, and without retribution—being utterly free from words and letters.
“World-Honored One!
All dharmas are likewise thus.
If a bodhisattva knows this, it is called skillfully knowing the nature of all dharmas and attaining the patience of non-arising.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja spoke this dhāraṇī, saying: "Aṇu-nai-pi-bha-ra-ja-ma-aṇu-ca-ya-si-nai-si-nai."
Jaṇa-vimuni-munīhara-ānaya-phala-kuha-garbha-nirvaha-suvi-vini-śāsana-pa.
Śanama śanāḍu, taṭa-maṇa-madu, vaṃ viśa-śaha-śama-cīḍa-na-kī-ri-śa-aṅgu-pu-du-saṃśu-sra-ni svāhā. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”
You have now spoken this Inexhaustible Subduing Lion’s Play Dhāraṇī.

At the time of death, when the final consciousness of all sentient beings is beset by heavy afflictive obstructions and grave evil karma, this dhāraṇī is able to incinerate them all, enabling them to be reborn in a pure Buddha-land.

"Noble son! You are now well able to bring immeasurable sentient beings to maturity by this means; you can also bring to maturity all sentient beings in the villages, gardens, cities, and towns of immeasurable Buddha-fields. Furthermore, you manifest various forms according to what is appropriate, and you preach various dharmas according to their faculties, or expound Mahāyāna sūtras to open the gates of the profound Dharma."

If there are śramaṇa-cāṇḍālas, brahmin-cāṇḍālas, kṣatriya-cāṇḍālas, vaiśya-cāṇḍālas, or śūdra-cāṇḍālas—the heavy offenses committed by all such persons as these have been entirely incinerated because of you, and they now establish themselves in and increase their wholesome dharmas.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“The various greed and disputes of sentient beings All arise because of the sense faculties;
If one can restrain these sense faculties, One will swiftly attain liberation.”

At that time, when the Tathāgata had finished preaching this sutra, ten thousand humans and devas attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*); immeasurable humans and devas attained various samādhis; furthermore, immeasurable humans and devas attained dhāraṇīs; moreover, immeasurable humans and devas attained forbearance (*kṣānti*); and yet more immeasurable humans and devas each made progress within the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*).
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, saying:
"You all should reverently receive and uphold this sutra.
Thereupon, Ānanda and the Bodhisattva Maitreya rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, knelt with their right knees on the ground, joined their palms, and said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
I have already received and upheld this sublime sūtra.
What should this sūtra be named?”
The Buddha said, “Good son!

This sutra is titled ‘The Dhāraṇī Sutra on Repenting and Exhausting All Sins. It is also titled ‘The Sutra on the Inconceivable Wisdom of Expedient Means for Rescuing and Delivering All Sentient Beings. It is also titled ‘The Sutra on Being Able to Fulfill All the Wishes of Sentient Beings Like a Wish-Fulfilling Jewel. It is also titled ‘The Sutra of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.’”
Thus should you uphold it.

Ānanda, you should know that if there are sons or daughters of good family who have long since resolved their minds on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas have practiced the six *pāramitās*, making various kinds of offerings at the abodes of all Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions, even until the completion of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;

It is not as good as for someone to read, recite, copy, explain to others, and uphold the name of the *Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva Sūtra*. Compared to the former merit, it does not equal even a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred-thousand-millionth part; it is beyond the reach of calculation or analogy.
At that time, Ānanda and Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We shall uphold it in this manner.”
At that time, the great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced with leaping joy and made offerings to the Buddha with various ritual implements.
*The Sutra of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha*.
